description: TCC monitoring and control of 146 transmission substations and about 5,900 circuit miles; switching, contingency analysis, ICCP data exchange with the Reliability Coordinator and Balancing Authority
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: NERC TOP obligations require continuous monitoring and control; loss of the EMS without transfer to the backup TCC risks BES instability and a reportable event (EOP-004-4 complete loss of monitoring or control for 30 minutes; DOE-417 criterion 26 for a system report)
manual_workaround: Transfer to the backup TCC (last exercise 48 minutes); Reliability Coordinator monitoring as a backstop; field staffing of Substations P, R, and K with direct phone control
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-05; SYS-08 (EMS domain); SYS-12 (Intermediate Systems)
dependent_third_parties: EMS vendor; telecom carriers (ICCP circuits); Reliability Coordinator; Balancing Authority
dependent_people_or_facilities: 96 TCC operators and engineers; TCC; backup TCC at OCN
quantified_impact_basis: Regulatory exposure (NERC penalties up to the statutory maximum per day per violation), restoration cost, and lost sales if transmission contingencies cause load loss; estimated planning value for a 24-hour EMS loss with backup TCC running at reduced capability
nerc_cip_scope: High impact BES Cyber Systems (EMS); CIP-012-2 for ICCP
single_points_of_failure: Single EMS vendor; ICCP to the RC carried over one carrier entrance at the backup TCC (gap 7)

description: Real-time monitoring and control of 3,380 feeders: switching, FLISR, volt-VAR optimization, clearances, TOP-directed manual load shedding through the ADMS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Worker safety (clearances and switching orders), public safety (downed wire response), and TOP-directed load shed capability; on a summer peak day about 1.95 million meters depend on DCC switching
manual_workaround: Paper switching orders and radio dispatch; field operation of substation breakers; FLISR disabled (longer outages); backup DCC at OCN (failover test 5 h 20 min against a 2 h RTO)
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-04; SYS-12; SYS-08 (ADMS domain)
dependent_third_parties: ADMS vendor (support and remote access); telecom carriers; private LTE vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 210 DCC operators and engineers; DCC at the GOC; backup DCC at OCN
quantified_impact_basis: Restoration and overtime cost about $1.4 million, lost sales about $0.9 million, and customer credits and regulatory exposure about $1.3 million for a day without remote switching during a normal weather day; much higher in a storm
nerc_cip_scope: Outside CIP scope (2024 compliance memo); OT-STD-01 voluntary CIP-equivalent
single_points_of_failure: Single ADMS instance with warm standby; 4 ADMS jump hosts are the only engineer path

description: Outage prediction from AMI and calls, crew dispatch to 4,100 mobile tablets, estimated restoration times, medical-priority customer handling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Restoration speed (reliability indices reported to state commissions); medical-priority customers; storm restoration where outages can exceed 500,000 customers
manual_workaround: Paper trouble tickets and radio dispatch; spreadsheet storm tracker; outage map frozen at last update
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-02; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-09 (GIS on Cloud A)
dependent_third_parties: OMS vendor; mobile carrier; GIS platform (Cloud provider A)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Dispatchers; storm command center; 4,900 field staff
quantified_impact_basis: Slower restoration (about 30% longer outages), crew overtime, mutual assistance holding costs, and customer credits on a normal day; storm days far higher
single_points_of_failure: OMS warm standby at OCN has never carried storm load

business_process: Customer contact center and IVR (including outage and hazard reporting)
description: About 52,000 calls a day (up to 600,000 in a hurricane): downed wire and hazard reports, outage reporting, billing and payment calls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Public safety: hazard calls (downed wires, gas smell referrals) must reach the DCC; outage reporting volume in storms
manual_workaround: Overflow to the outsourced contact center and Utility Services agents; hazard calls routed to a direct DCC line; IVR outage messages only
dependent_third_parties: Contact center platform vendor (SaaS); telephony carriers; outsourced overflow contact center
quantified_impact_basis: Hazard response delays and abandoned calls; agent idle time and overflow vendor premium; complaints to state commissions

description: Storm command center, mutual assistance, crew logistics, critical facility restoration lists, public and regulator communications
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Activated for hurricanes and major storms; a cyber event during a storm multiplies impact; state commission and emergency management reporting
manual_workaround: Paper incident command forms; satellite phones; manual crew tracking
dependent_third_parties: Mutual assistance utilities; logistics vendors; satellite communications provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Storm command center at the GOC; Georgia Operations Center; 38 district centers
quantified_impact_basis: Planning value for a storm day with degraded command systems: extended restoration, mutual assistance crew standby (about 3,000 external workers), and regulatory scrutiny
single_points_of_failure: Storm command center co-located with the DCC at the GOC

description: Telemetry and control paths to 418 distribution substations, 146 transmission substations, and about 41,000 field devices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Loss of telemetry blinds the DCC and TCC to field conditions; protection keeps working locally because relays trip on their own
manual_workaround: Field crews staff key substations; manual readings by radio; protection operates locally
dependent_third_parties: Private LTE vendor; licensed radio vendor; telecom carriers
quantified_impact_basis: Crew staffing of substations, delayed restoration, and loss of remote switching
nerc_cip_scope: Medium impact at Substations P, R, K; low impact at 143 transmission substations; distribution substations outside CIP scope
single_points_of_failure: Private LTE core is a single vendor service

business_process: Physical security and access control for control centers and substations
description: Badge and alarm systems for CIP Physical Security Perimeters, substations, and control centers; 24x7 security operations desk
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: CIP-006-6 requires alarms to reach incident responders within 15 minutes and entry logging; CIP-014-3 physical security plan for Substation P
manual_workaround: Guard posts at the TCC and Substation P; manual entry logs; temporary escorts
dependent_systems: Physical access control system (PACS) servers at DC-1 and DC-2; camera and intrusion detection systems
quantified_impact_basis: Guard posts and manual logging, plus regulatory exposure for CIP-006 alarm and logging requirements
nerc_cip_scope: PACS associated with high and medium impact BES Cyber Systems
single_points_of_failure: PACS servers patched by one vendor-certified technician

business_process: Wholesale power scheduling and load forecasting
description: Day-ahead and hourly schedules, PPA dispatch instructions, load forecasts (AI-001), settlements with the Balancing Authority and counterparties
process_owner: Director, Power Supply and Load Forecasting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Day-ahead submission deadline each morning; missed or poor schedules create imbalance charges (about $400,000 normal day, up to $3 million peak day)
manual_workaround: Prior-day schedule adjusted for weather; counterparty forecast; manual schedule entry by phone
dependent_systems: SYS-16 (AI-001 on Cloud provider B); SYS-01 (historian replica); SYS-06 (aggregated AMI data); SYS-11
dependent_third_parties: Weather data provider; Balancing Authority scheduling system; PPA counterparties
quantified_impact_basis: Imbalance charges on a typical summer day plus scheduling penalties
single_points_of_failure: One weather data provider; model run by a team of 4

description: About 6,500 remote connects and disconnects a day for move-ins, move-outs, and nonpayment, plus emergency disconnects for fires
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers waiting for service at move-in; misuse of bulk disconnect could cut power to up to 50,000 meters per command (gap 4)
manual_workaround: Field crews perform connects; disconnections for nonpayment paused
quantified_impact_basis: Truck rolls for manual connects (about $70 each) and delayed move-ins
single_points_of_failure: AMI head-end is a single vendor SaaS

business_process: Meter data management and billing determinants
description: Collection and validation of interval data from 1.95 million meters; billing determinants to the CIS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Meters store about 45 days of interval data, so data is recoverable; billing windows set the outer limit
manual_workaround: Estimated reads under tariff rules; backfill from meter storage

description: Bill calculation and delivery for about 2.1 million active accounts, including deposits and credit decisions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash flow (about $12.5 million of billed revenue per day); state rules on billing timeliness
manual_workaround: Delay bill runs; estimate bills; hold late fees
dependent_third_parties: Bill print and mail vendor; Cloud provider A
quantified_impact_basis: Financing cost on deferred cash and rework; the cash itself is delayed, not lost

description: Payment processing through the processor hosted page, IVR, lockbox, and walk-in agents; deposits based on consumer reports; collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers cannot pay (disconnection rules must then be suspended); posting errors
manual_workaround: Lockbox and agent payments posted later; disconnections for nonpayment suspended
dependent_third_parties: Payment processor; lockbox bank; consumer reporting agency; collection agency
quantified_impact_basis: About 17% of daily receipts delayed past due date, waived fees, and suspended collections
single_points_of_failure: Single payment processor for card and bank payments

description: Account access, payments, outage reporting and status, usage data
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 60% of outage reports and payments come through digital channels; reputation in storms
manual_workaround: Contact center and IVR take the load
dependent_systems: SYS-07; SYS-09 (Cloud provider B mobile back end); SYS-08
dependent_third_parties: Cloud providers A and B; customer identity service
quantified_impact_basis: Higher call volume and agent overtime; complaints
single_points_of_failure: Customer identity service shared by portal and app

description: CIS hosting, billing, MDM, and outage call overflow for 7 client utilities (about 410,000 meters)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client contracts: 99.9% monthly availability, 8-hour RTO, 15-minute RPO, 5% monthly fee credit per missed service level; the company is the clients third-party agent for customer data
manual_workaround: Client utilities defer billing and use their own call centers
quantified_impact_basis: Fee credits (about $210,000 per missed service level per month), client remediation, and contract risk at 2027 renewals
single_points_of_failure: Shares the CIS platform with the company

description: Managed charging for 62 fleet and municipal clients: charger operations, session authorization, energy reporting, billing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Fleet vehicles must charge overnight for next-day routes; client service levels promise 4-hour restoration of charging management
manual_workaround: Chargers run in offline mode with local authorization lists for up to 72 hours; manual session reconciliation
dependent_third_parties: Charging management SaaS vendor (subservice organization); cellular carrier
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits, client fleet disruption, and reputation in a growing line of business

business_process: Work, asset, and supply chain management
description: Work orders, materials, inventory for storms, asset records (ERP)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Materials for storms are staged in advance; outages slow capital work
manual_workaround: Paper work orders; printed storm material lists
dependent_people_or_facilities: Supply chain and work management staff
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed capital work and expediting costs

description: Pay for 12,000 employees and storm overtime
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Union agreements and state wage laws; storm overtime spikes

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual SEC filings, SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; the MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end window
manual_workaround: Manual journal entries with controller review
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and filing risk; reputational impact of a late filing is severe

business_process: NERC and DOE event reporting and compliance
description: EOP-004 event reports, DOE-417 filings, CIP-008 notifications, CIP evidence collection and SERC submissions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reporting clocks of 1 hour (DOE-417 Emergency Alert; CIP-008 Reportable Cyber Security Incident) are met by phone and paper forms when systems are down
manual_workaround: Phone notice to the DOE Operations Center and the E-ISAC; paper DOE-417 form; evidence rebuilt from system logs
dependent_people_or_facilities: NERC compliance team; DCC and TCC shift supervisors
quantified_impact_basis: Regulatory exposure for late filings rather than direct cost
